target_customer: Designers at launch, then Fortune 500 and government training teams
problem: Building AR and VR environments needed Unity or Epic tools that were powerful but very technical; Sketchbox let non coders design inside VR, then pivoted to VR training and assessment.
business_model: B2B SaaS for VR training simulations (enterprise and government)
product_category: VR / AR creation and training platform

founders.name: Joe Connolly
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder of Sketchbox (W18) and Greensky Games and as a former founder.

founders.name: Peter Le Bek
founders.background_notes: Described by Connolly in an interview as having built most of Sketchbox (per search snippet of a Medium interview); YC lists him as a former founder.

competitors.name: Unity
competitors.what: Established game engine used to build VR and AR environments, powerful but very technical

competitors.name: Epic Games (Unreal Engine)
competitors.what: Established game engine used to build VR and AR environments, powerful but very technical

technical_complexity.rationale: A 3D authoring tool that works inside VR headsets (Vive, Rift) with export to Unity and Sketchfab, later multi user VR sessions, analytics and an AI engine.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise integrations and LMS links help, but VR creation tools from Google and others were free or growing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company still operates per its site in 2026.

market_need_then: Designers without 3D skills found Unity and Unreal too technical, per TechCrunch February 2018; later enterprise demand for VR training appears in Air Force and Fortune 500 customers named on the site.

branding.domain_note: Uses sketchbox3d.com, adding 3D to the name; the USPTO mark SKETCHBOX is held by an unrelated company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Early tagline: Wordpress for AR and VR

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'Wordpress for AR & VR' on the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch coverage in 2018 and enterprise customer logos, but the name outgrew the sketching pitch and no brand community was found.

pivots.from: VR design tool for designers without code
pivots.to: VR training and assessment platform for enterprises and government
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC page and company site show the shift, but no date or reason.

outcome_analysis: Sketchbox started as a no code VR design tool and moved to enterprise VR training with named customers such as the U.S. Air Force, and its site is live with a 2026 copyright even though YC marks it inactive. Funding beyond a small seed is unclear, and the cause of any stall is not public.
notes: Status conflict: YC says Inactive but the company website still operates in 2026. The 120k seed (Feb 2018) rests on a single database (CB Insights), which also says 620k raised over 3 rounds, so two rounds are missing; Alphagrowth lists seed dates of Nov 2017, Mar 2018 and Apr 2018 without amounts. The TechCrunch article names Unity and Epic Games only as the established tools Sketchbox contrasts itself with. Exit type none reflects the live site; YC status may be stale.
